claims.text: In-situ oxidation testing can be used to improve oxidation resistance in high-entropy alloys.
In-situ oxidation testing allows real-time monitoring of oxidation behavior.
Real-time oxidation monitoring can identify the most effective methods for achieving high oxidation resistance.
The proposed method applies to HEAs with varying compositions and microstructures.
The testing is to be performed under high-temperature conditions.
Protective oxide layers form during the proposed intervention.
Formation of protective oxide layers mediates oxidation resistance.
Real-time monitoring enables relationships among composition, processing, and oxidation resistance to be identified.
In-situ oxidation testing will produce improved oxidation resistance in HEAs.
The proposed approach is applicable to extreme environments involving high temperatures and radiation.

contradictions.description: In-situ oxidation testing is presented as an observational/diagnostic method, but it is also treated as if its presence directly causes protective oxide formation and improved oxidation resistance. The mechanism only explains acquisition of information, not a material modification that would make tested HEAs more oxidation resistant than untested controls.
